purpose: Replace the body-like hump with an unmistakable near/front pectoral fin and keep the farther fin hidden.

arguments.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: transparent production cartoon sprite
Input images: Image 1 is the edit target, current selected SLEVEJM2.BMP frame 009; Image 2 is the enlarged nearest-neighbor original pose reference; Image 3 is the native pixel original pose reference.
Primary request: Replace the current raised near-side appendage with an unmistakable shark pectoral fin performing the same original gesture.
Subject detail: The shark is upright in the water. The ONE visible fin must be the near/front pectoral fin. Its broad base must visibly emerge from the near chest/shoulder just behind the gill area, then extend toward image-right and taper to one pointed fin tip with a slightly downward curve, matching the original reference gesture. It must read as a flat triangular pectoral fin, not a rounded arm, body swelling, shoulder lump, dorsal hump, or back hump.
Style/medium: polished 2D hand-inked cartoon sprite matching Image 1 exactly
Composition/framing: keep the shark pose, crop, scale, orientation, facial expression, waterline, and transparent canvas from Image 1
Constraints: change only the fin anatomy and its local attachment; hide the farther pectoral fin completely; preserve the dorsal fin and entire back silhouette; preserve shark identity, gray palette, white belly, outlines, highlights, face, teeth, gills, and water splash; genuinely transparent background; no added objects; no text; no watermark
Avoid: second pectoral fin; detached fin; fin attached to the back; rounded hump; arm or hand anatomy; extra limb; changed face; changed body silhouette outside the near chest attachment
